title: cli: `os db orphans --delete` and `os secret orphans --delete` in a non-interactive shell without `--yes` delete nothing, print "Aborted", and exit 0 — the migrate family exits 1
body:
repo:objectstack#4 · os-project-manager · session_01FEkQ5oY5WCqqqBMtn9qt7m

## What happens

`os db orphans --delete --export FILE` and `os secret orphans --delete --export FILE`, run without `--yes` where stdin is not a terminal (a script, CI, a cron job), print `Aborted — no export was written and no row was deleted.` and return exit 0. A script reads success; nothing was deleted.

Read from source on main (reach not measured at a running deployment):

- `packages/cli/src/commands/db/orphans.ts:233-236` — text face: `const ok = await confirm(...)`; `if (!ok) { printInfo('Aborted — ...'); return; }` (exit 0). The `--json` face of the same branch already exits 1 with `confirmation_required`.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/secret/orphans.ts:398` — the same shape.
- The shared `confirm` answers `false` when `!process.stdin.isTTY` (`packages/cli/src/commands/db/orphans.ts:402`, "non-interactive → require --yes").

## Why it is a defect

The `os migrate` family settled this in #24949: a run that did not get its confirmation applies nothing and exits 1, naming `--yes`; `packages/cli/test/migrate-confirmation-exit.pin.test.ts` pins it, but its roster reads only `src/commands/migrate/**`, so the two `orphans --delete` commands are outside it. Found while dispatching PR #36304 (`os migrate list-preferences`, which joined that roster).

## Done when

- Both commands, text face, non-TTY, no `--yes`: exit 1 with a line naming `--yes`; nothing exported or deleted (as today).
- An interactive "no" answer may stay exit 0 or follow the migrate family: the dev reads how the family treats it and matches it.
- A pin covers both commands (extending the confirmation pin's population, or a sibling pin), with an ablation.

Out of scope: any change to what the commands delete or export.

Precedent: #24949.
